title: Shank 2
text: I played the original Shank some years ago on Xbox Live Arcade and didn't get around to playing the sequel until fairly recently. While I am disappointed that the co-op campaign of the first game was replaced with a mere wave survival mode in this one, the single player campaign delivers the same sort of experience as the first, a beer-soaked, white-knuckle, bullet-riddled rampage through a grindhouse version of South America, and that's nothing to complain about. I would best describe Shank 2 as a 2D "Stylish Action Game", a term that never really caught on, since people think God of War invented this style of gameplay when, really, Devil May Cry did it first- and better. To be fair, the Shanks are closer in style to God of War, and though there is a combo grading system in the game you can get by perfectly well by mashing the buttons until you have smeared your enemies into the pavement. Shank 2 delivers fast, brutal action, varied weapons and cinematic boss battles, and despite the short length of the game it is excellently paced and good fun to play throughout. I hope this is not the last we have seen of our headbanded hero and his messy adventures.

title: Shantae and the Pirate's Curse
text: Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is a 2D metroidvania platformer adventure. You play as Shantae, the half genie guardian of Scuttle Town. Recently you have lost your magical powers, but you don't let that stop you from saving the town once trouble comes through. Most of the trouble is caused by evil magic being sent out by the imprisoned spirit of the Master Pirate. It's your job to team up with your former rival Risky Boots in order to stop his minions, collect the magic, and prevent his spirit's escape. The gameplay is fairly simple. You can run around, jump, duck, crawl, and whip your hair to attack. Along the way you will receive new items and upgrades to give yourself more abilities and more power. You use these abilities to access new areas in order to find secrets and progress. There are a few light puzzles and fetch quests sprinkled in, but the main play will consist of traversing overworlds and conquering dungeons. You can also increase your health and carry items to heal you on the go or to give you some other battle assistance. You'll need to skilled in combat, platforming, and adventuring to complete this game. The music is overall pretty great, being polished and interesting to listen to. The art is a mixture of two styles. The playable game consists of colorful pixel art that is well animates, while the dialogue bits have hand drawn cartoonish representations of the characters. The sound effects are also an interesting mix of higher quality voice and sound sample along with retro style video gamey effects. The controls are tight and understandable. Plus, the dialogue is cute and can actually be funny at time. It's an interesting mixture. For those who played Shantae: Risky's Revenge before this as I did, you'll be glad to know that nearly everything has been improved upon in this game. You get lots of new abilities rather than just recollecting the same ones from the previous game. The story is even more interesting with the same quality of dialogue. The hand drawn art is different, but it seems to have a bit more detail. This game has more length, with more places to explore, things to do, things to find, people to talk to, and just generally more everything, which means even more quality playtime. The difficulty is also higher for those looking for a greater challenge, which is welcome since this is a sequel, but not too hard for newcomers that would like to try it as well. The map system has been improved to read more like a standard metroidvania style map and show you where you have and have not been. If you liked exploring, platforming challenges, puzzle challenges, combat challenges, and just the overall gameplay of the previous game, you'll love this one even more. There are a few issues with the game though. One that may have just been for me was that sometimes there was a flickering glitchy effect on some backgrounds. This usually only happened in the company logo right away and on the world selection screen, but it also did happen consistently in one temple where I kind of needed to know where the walls and floors were. It was only for that one room in the one temple, but it kept happening after a few reloads so it may be a real problem for others as well. Also, I didn't think the cartoonish characters hand drawn in dialogue scenes meshed well with the pixel style of the game. Mayb it's just me, but I would rather just keeping it all one way. That's minor. The difficulty could be a problem. It's harder than the previous game, which is good for people who played that first and it's not TOO hard for those who want to jump right in, but to some casual gamers it could be a bit too tough to get through. While I like that the map system has been reworked and the sailing aspect works will with giving Risky more purpose, it's a shame that instead of one big interconnected world it's now multiple smaller worlds you have to select separately. Overall, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is awesome. If you like metroidvania games, it's a great one. If you played the previous game (which I also reviewed on here) and liked it, this is definitely worth looking into. It's a fun, metroidvania adventure platformer with a pretty style. I like how fun, challenging, and yet forgiving the game is to make it a lot of fun to keep playing. Another one of the best games I've played on Steam. Is it worth the 20 dollar asking price? Well, personally I would say that, if you're really interested and liked the other Shantae games, then of course. Otherwise maybe wait for a sale. I got it for 15 and it was worth not being able to wait anymore. If nothing else, getting it at 10 bucks or less at some point is going to be a real steal, especially for all the content here. Shantae and the Pirate's Curse gets a 9 out of 10 for being a great blend of genres, gameplay, personality, and style. Also... I know I'm a pervert but... I mean, come on, Shantae is a babe ;)

title: Shantae and the Pirate's Curse
text: Ahoy! WayForward's trademark heroine is back with a new adventure that will see her join forces with her sworn enemy Risky Boots, and swap her (half-)genie moves with a brand spanking new pirate arsenal. Much like its , is a casual adventure platformer with a charming cartoonish design. As per usual, the new abilities you unlock as the story progresses go hand in hand with increasingly challenging foes and level design. Although some backtracking will at times break the linearity, the game follows a stable pattern of unlocking new areas one after another, each of which will feature some sort of maze-like dungeon where you'll earn a new skill and fight a boss. Although the difficulty increases with each new area, it remains relatively easy on the whole, meaning you'll probably clear this ten-hour adventure without much frustration (only the final dungeon has a few brutal screens). If you've done a good job of amassing health upgrades, the boss fights are pretty straightforward and a wise use of the healing/shielding/offensive items will help keep you alive. None of them are hugely challenging, although the achievements for defeating them without taking damage are another story. With the gameplay relying on rather classic action platformer mechanics and only posing a moderate challenge, its true highlights lie elsewhere. The cartoonish design is just delightful, most notably in the dialogue scenes where the character art is all kinds of cute. The writing is tons of fun, with heaps of absurd comedy, mild innuendo and occasionally breaking the fourth wall, all the same ingredients that had already made the previous episode so refreshing. text: This game is a great step forward for the series, and the previous entry was already pretty good. The new semi-3D graphics look awesome and are put to great use. Shantae gets a lot of forms and they all feel more organic and useful than they did in Risky's Revenge (probably thanks to the level design). Zelda-dungeons have been replaced with more megaman-style linear levels, which you could go either way on; my feeling is that the levels are much more fun and tightly-paced, and they have much better setpieces. There is a lot of mandatory backtracking, but it's not any worse than the previous games (especially if you get the warp dance). Usually by the time it wants you to return to a level a few new enemies have been added you have new forms to find hidden items in it. The only criticism I can think of is that the story is kinda all-over-the-place. Instead of pursuing an overarching "gather X plot coupons" goal you jump back and forth between unrelated plotlines that each last one level, while occasionally fetching an item for your uncle's machine from a previous level. But it still has fun characters and cute dialog, so it's ok.

title: Shantae: Half-Genie Hero
text: TL;DR: A wonderus harmony of what could well be some of the best platforming, exploration, and FUN I've ever had! I'm a gamer of over 25 years, and this game is simply AMAZING! New features: More direct level designs, a fresh "2.5D" graphics engine with HD support (4k+), AMAZING animation,  fun and memorable soundtrack you'll be humming all day long, and 10+ hours of gameplay. Super cute characters, PG-13 animated boobies on nearly everything, and nearly everything dances! Oh, and it's NOT a frustrating roguelike! Long review: Graphics: 10/10. Supports 4k+ resoutions. Beautifully animated (hand-drawn, not "flash game" type), "2.5D" graphics. Everything is bouncy, round, wiggly, jiggly, and FULL OF LIFE! Such talent and effort! Even the backgrounds are animated, every enemy, all the widgets, everything! If I could give an 11, I would! Thank you for raising the bar on what a modern platformer should look like! Sound/music: 10/10. Beautiful, level-matching, custom soundtrack with loop points, an energetic song with vocals, fresh and original. A TON of effort was put into this soundtrack! Quality over quantity, every song is unique and very memorable! I LOVE THE SNARE IN MERMAID FALLS (a'la Sonic 2)! Controls: 10/10. Accurate, precise, fast and responsive movements. Flawless and natural feeling with a gamepad! Gameplay: 10/10. Everything in the game "fits" and has a purpose. The level design is top-notch, reminiscent of games of old; nearly every level is like an onion, with multiple layers depending on your current abilities. They're not too mazey, not frustrating, yet they're challenging and clever. FUN BOSSES that aren't too frustrating or difficult! You never really get tired of revisitng a level and searching for treasures unfound. The only notch off a perfect score is the transformation selection system: it's NOT BAD, don't get me wrong, I didn't DISLIKE it, but it felt a bit out-of-place in this finely polished gem of a game. Noticeable when you need to change often in a level. I would have prefered a right-analog-stick menu, but I understand the choice that compromised between keyboard, non-stick gamepads, and xbox-style gamepads. Story: 6/10. It's very fun and gives the game a way-better-than-most-platformers plot device. It's not going to bring you to tears or make you think about philosophy or anything beyond providing a fun plot device for the game to progress on. Game Length: 8/10. I got about 10 hours out of my first playthrough, and managed 92% item completion. At the end, I was hoping for one last uber-boss to appear, becasue that would've been perfect. I haven't played the other modes as of this review (2/20/17), but I'll give them a try and see how long I can actually stretch this game out to. Overall: 9/10. Buy this game, it's EASILY worth $20. You'd be hard-pressed to get a meal for two for that amount, a couple coffees, or a boquet of flowers. The developers put thousands of hours (cumulative) into this game, requiring decades of talent and learning; and it shows BIG time! EXCELLENT JOB! Final thoughts: I've been playing platformers hardcore since the early 90's. I like some platformers, and I dislike others. I like my platformers to be challenging yet fun (like Mario 3 or Sonic 2), or deep and immersive Metroidvania 40+ hour games. This game filled my "challenging yet fun" bucket FULL of candy!  I dislike games like Megaman, I Wanna Be the Guy, or most "that's a game mechanic, not a glitch" type games. I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Everything about it is fun, detailed and engaging. I love the new engine, and the animations stand out in the best way possible. I like the "like an onion" level designs, and I wish every level had the same depth that Mermaid Falls had, even if it were for some pointless loot and a completion percentage. I wanted to use the mouse (transformation) and spider a little more! I REALLY like how the levels are shorter, much less mazey, and don't require a minimap to navigate. Thanks for an immediately amazing, thoroughly fun and extremely well-produced game!

And most importantly of all, do you enjoy the frustration of wasting tonnes of harpoon gun ammo TRYING to shoot sharks at close range and completely failing?  If you answered "yes" to at least two of the above, Shark Attack Deathmatch 2 may be just the game you've been waiting for.  I am, of course, just being a bitter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, so in acknowledgement of the fact that there's maybe a few people out there talented enough to actually stay alive longer than five to ten minutes in this hard-as-all-♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥er of a game, I'll mention some of its good features.  The graphics are awesome, the maps are genuinely interesting - hell, even occasionally inspired (sunken New York, anyone?) - and the sound is awesome, too.  On the whole, the atmosphere is absolutely fantastic and the underwater worlds perfectly immersive.  The problem?  Well, maybe there isn't one.  Or more to the point, maybe the problem is ME.  Rival game Depth at least attempted to be SLIGHTLY more than a "deathmatch", but true enough to its title, that's literally all this one seems to be. Well, that and a "survival mode", which as we all know is just gamer lingo for "single-player deathmatch".  Man, I so badly want someone to make one of these first-person, scary shark games with a STORY.  If you make a game like that, and make it as GOOD as this and Depth admittedly manage to be, I WILL MARRY YOU AND HAVE YOUR BABIES.  Even if you're a dude.  Hell, I'll even be the woman, if such a compromise has to be made. What the ♥♥♥♥ is with the uber-popularity of all these multiplayer games, anyway?  Don't any of you people like YOURSELVES?  Or do you just not have any REAL-WORLD FRIENDS?  WHY CAN'T SOMEONE MAKE A TOTALLY ♥♥♥♥ING AWESOME SINGLE-PLAYER SHARK GAME?!  I love games.  I love sharks (well, okay, only in a they-totally-scare-the-bejesus-out-of-me way, but you know what I mean).  I WANT A SCARY, TENSE SHARK GAME WHICH ISN'T A DEATHMATCH.  Oh, and before all you clever♥♥♥♥♥♥♥start asking me why I bought a game with "deathmatch" in the title just to write a review complaining that the game IS a deathmatch, for the record, a friend gifted me this.  And even after the semi-disappointment of Depth, I was still excited to start 'er up.  But upon finding that this was considerably HARDER than Depth, and attempting to consolidate this with the equally indisputable fact that I'm basically pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥at video games, I have to say that I'm going to declare Depth my favourite of the two games.  If for no reason other than the fact that I actually managed to KILL some sharks in that one.  Which is a pretty cool thing to be able to do in a shark-killing game, right? And yeah yeah yeah, I know that's just a cue for all you smart ♥♥♥♥ers to point out that if I only exercised a little patience, or failing that simply (and not to mention magically) "get gud" at the game, I might achieve my holy grail and actually KILL A ♥♥♥♥ING SHARK.  But you know what?  Right now I really couldn't be ♥♥♥♥ed.  And I'm on mutha♥♥♥♥in' HOLIDAYS at the moment, so that's surely gotta be sayin' somethin'...  In conclusion, definitely recommended to anyone who fancies themselves any good at these kinds of games, or indeed to anyone who just fancies a quick, immersive dive into a truly believable underwater kingdom before being unceremoniously "murdered by a shark" (the game's words, not mine).  With little doubt, the best shark-feeding simulator liable to be released on Steam this year. Oh, and PS...good luck finding a multiplayer game to actually JOIN.  I think I managed to CREATE such a game, but alas, I was the only thing remotely resembling a HUMAN BEING in it.  But I guess it is only in Early Access, so with a little luck we'll see that particular comment of mine become null-and-void in the near future.  I have a suspicion I will revisit these waters, sooner or later, but for now the ♥♥♥♥ing sharks can just go hungry.  FINNED, FISHY ♥♥♥♥ERS.  Verdict: 7/10.

text: One of the few games of this kind, was really interested in picking it up after playing a lot of Depth so I wanted to try something else, unfortunately, it's DOA. This is a multiplayer focused game and it's tumbleweeds everywhere, 100% barren, no-one is playing it, you can spend countless, fruitless minutes waiting for someone to join you in a game with no luck. And the single player portion is a joke and a bad one at that, as of right now it's just the survival mode which is just wave after wave of 2 or 3 not-so-smart sharks roaming around and that's it, really, nothing more than a badly disguised training mode. There are no bots, no other divers to shoot or compete with and no other modes, so it gets tiring and boring super fast. The few maps there are somewhat decent in the graphics department, especially the interesting Tsunami one featuring a flooded piece of Manhattan, but since the action is nowhere to be found you just explore them in a few mins and then you've seen everything there is to the game. The rest of the maps are pretty empty and small except for usually two big objects like say a sunken boat and a WWII bomber or some anti-ship mines floating around, not much to get excited about. If you're looking for some underwater action, get Depth instead or wait for a full release of this game before trying it out, till then... don't even bother. The most worrying thing with this title is that the description in the Steam page says it's BETA when there's not much content to begin with, it is playable for the little it has and I didn't encounter any issues while I played like some have complained but gameplay wise, again, there's just almost nothing to enjoy and what little there is it'll have to be by yourself, not anyone's idea of fun.

title: Sherlock Holmes: The Devil's Daughter
text: Recieved in the July Monthly Humble Bundle Games like this are a dream for people who love detective stories and just being detectives in general. The game does a good job of making you feel like Sherlock Holmes despite feeling a tad easy at certain points by guiding you on what to do, even on the "hard" difficulty. The cases aren't anything new or groundbreaking but are still interesting enough to leave you wanting more. Every case has multiple endings that the player can decide by coming up with deductions based on the evidence given; however, every case has correct deductions and inncorrect ones. Every outcome then has a moral choice that the player can decide between such as letting the suspect go because his motive gave him a just reason to commit the crime, etc. The game has a strange habit of throwing you into mini games and quick time events without really explaining why and how it works, but for the most part they are things that are somewhat common knowledge like shoe shining and lawn bowls, or just basic quick time events. The music is pretty nice and suits the game's atmosphere well but still isn't anything too memorable. If you're a sucker for detective games and if you can overlook all the tiny, sometimes questionable, details that fault this game then you will enjoy Sherlock Holmes: The Devil's Daughter.
